correctness.rationale: For fixed p and s, the uniform-vector block is the sample mean of iid Binomial(s,p) sink degrees, and the squared coupling to its orthogonal complement is their sample variance. The edge rank-one summands give the stated Bernstein variance proxy; the orthogonal internal block is pm times identity to relative o_P(1). Positivity and the Rayleigh upper bound give spectral separation, so the exact Schur complement yields m(B/m−xi) tending to sp(1−p)/p. This argument also proves the finite gap bracket. Binomial CLT and the o_P(n^−1/2) error prove the credited consequence, including strict window probabilities by continuity. Independent K5 test with z=(0,1,2,1,0): the lowest root below 5 of 2/(5−xi)+2/(6−xi)+1/(7−xi)=1 is 0.694102470667; the calculated Schur difference matches the eigenvalue difference 0.105897529333 to 1.25e−16. This is a finite check only. Supplied checker and verification notes were inspected, not executed.

evidence: Pirani–Sundaram Eq. (9) bounds the squared orthogonal deviation by 2sB/g² for the principal eigenvector normalized by max x_i=1. Their dense gap estimate gives ||d||=O_P(m^−1/2), and summing the eigenvector equation yields xi = B/m + z·d/(m gamma), gamma tending to 1.
This makes xi−B/m=O_P(m^−1); their binomial identification of B then implies the Gaussian window via the standard CLT. It does not evaluate m(B/m−xi).

value.rationale: The retained coefficient quantifies the first systematic error incurred by replacing the principal eigenvalue by the observed boundary mean. It verifies strict positive relaxation at a scale invisible to the Gaussian window and identifies how it depends on sink count and density. It is useful for assessed accuracy of the boundary-density approximation, not a claim about finite-population persistence.
